{
  "checks_performed": [
    "Read only the authorized source JSON and draft JSON; used no web access or other source files.",
    "Compared the draft’s conclusion against the exact target, which requires proving the limit is 1 or proving it is not 1.",
    "Derived the theta dual directly from SDP duality and checked its normalization and strong-duality conditions.",
    "Derived the complement-product inequality from the dual formulation and checked the exact complement-pair count.",
    "Checked the Gaussian comparison constants, Lipschitz constant, concentration exponent, and exact tail-moment integral.",
    "Checked the Rademacher-to-Gaussian closed-walk comparison term by term using exact even moments.",
    "Checked the signed dual certificate, Markov tail estimate, and asymptotic choices of k symbolically.",
    "Checked vertex-deletion Lipschitzness through Gram matrices and the variance and tail constants through the block-exposure martingale.",
    "Checked the exact complement identity and both directions of the variance/product-slack equivalence, including tail truncation and negative correlation.",
    "No claim depended on a finite numerical computation, so no checker program or floating-point decision was applicable."
  ],
  "claimed_resolution_verdict": "ACCURATE",
  "claims": [
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For every graph H, theta(H)=min lambda_max(M), where M ranges over real symmetric matrices satisfying M_ii=1 and M_ij=1 for every distinct nonedge ij of H. Also 1 <= theta(H) <= |V(H)|.",
      "claim_sha256": "de6162dda642d9e2eb591751bf990fdbb2b19a95e5462b405d39eda698faafbc",
      "evidence": "For every admissible M and primal-feasible X, <M,X>=<J,X> because M agrees with J on the diagonal and nonedges while X vanishes on edges. Hence <J,X>≤lambda_max(M)Tr(X). Conversely, the SDP Lagrange dual is min t subject to tI-M positive semidefinite with exactly those fixed entries; the strictly feasible primal point I/|V(H)| gives strong duality and dual attainment, and minimizing t for fixed M gives lambda_max(M). The matrix supported on one diagonal coordinate is primal-feasible with value 1, while J≤|V(H)|I in PSD order gives value at most |V(H)|.",
      "idx": 0,
      "search_method": "Direct SDP-duality and PSD-order proof.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "If μ_n=E theta(G_n) and N=binom(n,2), then μ_n >= sqrt(n)+(n+1-2sqrt(n))/2^N; in particular μ_n>sqrt(n) for every n>1.",
      "claim_sha256": "be33eb1e1337f590209f680c30c897f6a839946269e5c73aef1ce2893bb83eef",
      "evidence": "The complement inequality follows directly from claim 0: if t=theta(H), write tI-M as a Gram matrix of vectors b_i and set u_i=(1,b_i)/sqrt(t). The u_i are unit and orthogonal on nonedges of H, so their Gram matrix divided by n is feasible for theta(complement(H)); its objective is at least n/t from the common first coordinate. Thus theta(H)theta(complement(H))≥n. Complementation partitions the 2^N labeled graphs into pairs, each contributing at least 2sqrt(n). The empty/complete pair contributes n+1, an excess n+1-2sqrt(n), yielding the displayed mean bound after division by 2^N. The excess is (sqrt(n)-1)^2>0 for n>1.",
      "idx": 1,
      "search_method": "Symbolic complement-product derivation and exact complement-pair counting.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Let Z be symmetric with zero diagonal and independent standard Gaussian entries above the diagonal. For every integer k>=1, (E lambda_max(Z)^(2k))^(1/(2k)) <= 2sqrt(n)+2sqrt(k).",
      "claim_sha256": "2720f10cb1ed392e15eab15d4ec94b919fe8ece1cd7ad8110a9fcf7a6b9987fc",
      "evidence": "For unit x,y, X_x=x^T Zx satisfies E(X_x-X_y)^2=4 sum_{i<j}(x_ix_j-y_iy_j)^2≤4(1-(x·y)^2)≤8(1-x·y), which is the increment variance of Y_x=2g·x. Gaussian comparison therefore gives E lambda_max(Z)≤2E||g||≤2sqrt(n). As a function of the independent upper-triangular entries, lambda_max is sqrt(2)-Lipschitz, hence P(lambda_max-E lambda_max≥t)≤exp(-t^2/4). Because trace(Z)=0, lambda_max(Z)≥0. Exact tail integration gives E[(lambda_max-E lambda_max)_+^(2k)]≤4^k k!, whose 2k-th root is at most 2sqrt(k). Pointwise domination by the mean plus the positive deviation and Minkowski yield the claim.",
      "idx": 2,
      "search_method": "Gaussian increment comparison, Lipschitz concentration, and exact symbolic tail integration.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "Let W be symmetric with zero diagonal and independent uniform signs above the diagonal. For every integer k>=1, E lambda_max(W) <= (2n)^(1/(2k))(2sqrt(n)+2sqrt(k)).",
      "claim_sha256": "2069c6bd071c44ed9681523b3071ed2612db4e46362c38e5fd026ec45632ff36",
      "evidence": "In the closed-walk expansion of E Tr(W^(2k)), a loop-free term is 1 exactly when every unoriented edge has even multiplicity and is otherwise 0. The corresponding Gaussian term is then the integer product of double factorials (m_e-1)!!≥1, with the same zero pattern. Thus E Tr(W^(2k))≤E Tr(Z^(2k)). Every eigenvalue of Z has absolute value at most max(lambda_max(Z),lambda_max(-Z)), so E Tr(Z^(2k))≤2n E lambda_max(Z)^(2k). Claim 2 bounds this by 2n(2sqrt(n)+2sqrt(k))^(2k). Since trace(W)=0, lambda_max(W)≥0; its 2k-th power is at most Tr(W^(2k)), and the power-mean inequality proves the result.",
      "idx": 3,
      "search_method": "Exact closed-walk moment expansion and spectral power inequalities.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For every k>=1 and a>0, E theta(G_n) <= 1+(2n)^(1/(2k))(2sqrt(n)+2sqrt(k)), and P(theta(G_n)>1+a) <= 2n((2sqrt(n)+2sqrt(k))/a)^(2k). Consequently E theta(G_n) <= (2+o(1))sqrt(n), and for each fixed epsilon>0 the probability theta(G_n)>(2+epsilon)sqrt(n) is exp(-Omega_epsilon((log n)^2)).",
      "claim_sha256": "54fef16ba051e9f96d7c9a5d1df9588a8885b32e06150ff91cbfeb9478e8ee80",
      "evidence": "Assign W_ij=1 on nonedges and -1 on edges. Then W has independent uniform signs and M=I+W is admissible in claim 0, so theta(G_n)≤1+lambda_max(W). Claim 3 gives the expectation bound. If theta>1+a, then Tr(W^(2k))≥lambda_max(W)^(2k)>a^(2k); Markov's inequality and the exact moment comparison in claim 3 give the displayed probability. With k=ceil((log n)^2), (2n)^(1/(2k))=1+o(1) and sqrt(k)=o(sqrt(n)), proving the expectation asymptotic. For a=(2+epsilon)sqrt(n)-1, the ratio inside the tail bound tends to 2/(2+epsilon)<1, so its 2k-th power, even after the factor 2n, is exp(-Omega_epsilon((log n)^2)).",
      "idx": 4,
      "search_method": "Explicit theta-dual certificate, moment Markov bound, and symbolic asymptotic optimization.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "For every fixed epsilon>0, P((1/2-epsilon)sqrt(n) <= theta(G_n) <= (2+epsilon)sqrt(n)) tends to 1.",
      "claim_sha256": "781401f19b5f62a9507819d7ec3c3b023919e4193bfe1f371b69b93c4d326063",
      "evidence": "Claim 4 supplies the upper event with probability tending to one, both for G_n and its identically distributed complement. On theta(complement(G_n))≤(2+delta)sqrt(n), the complement-product inequality gives theta(G_n)≥sqrt(n)/(2+delta). For every fixed epsilon>0 one can choose delta>0 with 1/(2+delta)>1/2-epsilon. Intersecting this event with the upper event and applying a union bound proves the statement.",
      "idx": 5,
      "search_method": "Complement coupling, product inequality, and union bound.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "If H is obtained by deleting one vertex from G, then theta(H) <= theta(G) <= theta(H)+1. Consequently Var(theta(G_n)) <= (n-1)/4 and P(|theta(G_n)-μ_n|>=t) <= 2exp(-2t^2/(n-1)).",
      "claim_sha256": "85939397d2ac9626a308fb853ca9d055def3b39fa53db0677c03ff7205d3897b",
      "evidence": "Zero-padding a feasible matrix proves theta(H)≤theta(G). For a feasible Gram representation X_ij=<b_i,b_j>, let q=||b_v||^2 and s=sum_{i≠v}b_i. The restricted block has trace 1-q, so ||s||^2≤(1-q)theta(H). Hence the objective is at most (sqrt(q)+sqrt((1-q)theta(H)))^2≤1+theta(H) by Cauchy-Schwarz. Expose G_n through n-1 independent blocks, with block i containing its edges to earlier vertices. Replacing one block changes only edges incident to one vertex, and the deletion bound makes theta change by at most 1. The Doob conditional value has range at most 1 at each step; Hoeffding's lemma gives the stated two-sided bounded-difference tail, while Popoviciu's bound gives conditional variance at most 1/4. Orthogonality of martingale differences yields Var≤(n-1)/4.",
      "idx": 6,
      "search_method": "Gram-matrix restriction and an independent-block Doob martingale.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "With T_n=theta(G_n), T_n^c=theta(complement(G_n)), and μ_n=E T_n, the exact identity μ_n-sqrt(n)=(1/2)E[(sqrt(T_n)-sqrt(T_n^c))^2]+E[sqrt(T_n T_n^c)-sqrt(n)] holds, and both terms on the right are nonnegative.",
      "claim_sha256": "71896682313d8a766ab4e8720a5f7b5e7e2be0ba28dd0eb10252846911b3db9c",
      "evidence": "Expanding the square and using E T_n^c=E T_n=μ_n makes the right side equal μ_n-E sqrt(T_nT_n^c)+E sqrt(T_nT_n^c)-sqrt(n)=μ_n-sqrt(n). The squared term is nonnegative, and theta(G_n)theta(complement(G_n))≥n pointwise makes the second term nonnegative.",
      "idx": 7,
      "search_method": "Direct algebra and the complement-product inequality.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    },
    {
      "checker_path": "none",
      "claim": "The target limit μ_n/sqrt(n)->1 is equivalent to the conjunction Var(T_n)=o(n) and E[sqrt(T_nT_n^c)-sqrt(n)]=o(sqrt(n)).",
      "claim_sha256": "735bca015600f73d69d1a37ed31d6e8cc42cbb21213aee264db9218bbe994c13",
      "evidence": "By claim 7 and nonnegativity, the target limit is equivalent to product slack o(sqrt(n)) together with S_n=E[(sqrt(T_n)-sqrt(T_n^c))^2]=o(sqrt(n)). If Var(T_n)=o(n), equal marginal variances and Cauchy-Schwarz give E(T_n-T_n^c)^2≤4Var(T_n), while S_n≤E|T_n-T_n^c|; hence S_n=o(sqrt(n)). Conversely, fix C>2. On max(T_n,T_n^c)≤Csqrt(n), (T_n-T_n^c)^2≤4Csqrt(n)(sqrt(T_n)-sqrt(T_n^c))^2. Claim 4 makes the exceptional probability exp(-Omega((log n)^2)); since both theta values are at most n, its contribution to the squared difference is o(n). Thus S_n=o(sqrt(n)) implies E(T_n-T_n^c)^2=o(n). Finally T_n is decreasing and T_n^c increasing in every independent edge indicator, so the product-measure correlation inequality gives Cov(T_n,T_n^c)≤0. Therefore E(T_n-T_n^c)^2=2Var(T_n)-2Cov(T_n,T_n^c)≥2Var(T_n), proving Var(T_n)=o(n).",
      "idx": 8,
      "search_method": "Two-way moment comparison, exact tail truncation, and product-measure negative correlation.",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "witness": "none"
    }
  ],
  "complete": true,
  "confirmed_refutations": [],
  "iteration": 1,
  "overall": "VERIFIED",
  "parent_sha256": "61c80b5bc0b2dacc185eff8053c3992bf5f5d455a4e0b24ad2a764da7d6486f7",
  "record_id": "explore_random_graph_theta",
  "stage": "REVISION_AUDIT",
  "target_evidence": "The exact target asks for a proof that E[theta(G_n)]/sqrt(n) tends to 1 or a rigorous proof that the limit is not 1. The draft proves neither: it obtains the nonmatching constant bounds 1≤liminf≤limsup≤2, coarser high-probability bounds, and an equivalence reducing the desired limit to two further estimates, but it explicitly leaves both Var(T_n)=o(n) and asymptotic complement-product saturation unproved. Those bounds and the exact reduction are correct and material progress, so coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS rather than FULLY_RESOLVES_TARGET or NO_VALID_PROGRESS. Separately, the draft labels its resolution PARTIAL and its final writeup expressly says the target remains unresolved; that claimed resolution is ACCURATE and does not overstate coverage.",
  "target_verdict": "VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS",
  "arm": "plain"
}
